name: band-auth-card
description: A single-task account card on the page’s left edge: wordmark, one heading, two fields, one primary action, and the way back. For an account step AFTER sign-in (complete the profile, confirm a detail) — never the sign-in or sign-up door itself: the platform shows that screen.
provenPattern: Derived from a production account application: its auth shell, its destructive-action sections and its usage rows are the measured versions of these three arrangements.

knowledge.purpose: One account step the platform sign-in screen does not cover, asked on a page that offers nothing else: completing the profile after the first sign-in, or confirming one detail before the app continues. Sign-in, sign-up and password reset are shown by the PLATFORM when the app requires sign-in; this card is never that door.
useCases: Complete your profile after the first sign-in (contact e-mail, display name)
Confirm the address the app will write to before the first notification
Add the one detail an app needs before its first use (company, team)
antiPatterns: Using it as the app's own sign-in or sign-up screen — the platform owns that screen once the app requires sign-in; a page form that posts to /auth/login or asks for a password is a gate finding
Navigation around the card — every other destination is a way to lose the reader mid-task
Two primary actions on one card; neither is primary
A consent line with no address behind it — consent has to point at the version it consents to
Another h1 on the page: the title is the page's one h1 (this pattern is the whole task of its page); it keeps an h2's size

A submit that only flips page state — the step is written as the reader's own record (the entity declares an owner field `server: "owner"` and a "create, read own, update own" rule); the card reads it back, so a second visit edits the same record instead of adding one
A save that leaves without saying so — the card confirms what is now stored and keeps the way on
Centring the card in a wide page — it sits on the page’s left edge like the rest of the content; WIDTH keeps it narrow

One failure line for every refusal — the failure copy follows the write's reason (statusKeys.reason → {{state.submitReason}}: validation, unauthenticated, forbidden, conflict, network, server or error): the page's words for that reason, held in {{state.submitCopy}}, else the generic failure copy; the refused field names are in {{state.submitFields}}. The server's own words are never shown
A result nobody notices — the result (saved or failed) takes focus when it appears; every word on the card, the retry included, is the app’s

mobileCollapse: The card takes the full width minus the page gutter (or WIDTH, when given, on a wider screen); nothing else changes.

placeholders.{{TITLE}}: heading.text — the one task, e.g. Complete your profile
placeholders.{{SUBMIT}}: form.submitLabel — the single primary action, e.g. Save and continue
placeholders.{{ALT_LABEL}}: link.text — the way out, e.g. Do this later
placeholders.{{ALT_HREF}}: link.href — where the reader goes instead
placeholders.{{EMAIL_LABEL}}: input.label — the contact address, e.g. Contact e-mail
placeholders.{{DETAIL_LABEL}}: input.label — the one detail asked, e.g. Display name
placeholders.{{ENTITY}}: the app's entity type the step is saved to (e.g. Profile) — its fields take the form's names: email, detail; it declares an owner field (`server: "owner"`), so each reader sees and edits only their own
placeholders.{{FAILED_TEXT}}: alert.title when saving failed and no copy for its reason is given, e.g. That did not save — try again; plain text. The server's own words are never shown

{{FAILED_VALIDATION}}.description: the failure copy when the server refused one or more fields (400) — the refused field names are in {{state.submitFields}}, in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_UNAUTHENTICATED}}.description: the failure copy when the visitor is not signed in (401), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_FORBIDDEN}}.description: the failure copy when the visitor may not write this (403), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_CONFLICT}}.description: the failure copy when the record already exists (409, a unique field) — e.g. "You are already on the list", in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_NETWORK}}.description: the failure copy when nothing reached the server (no connection), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_SERVER}}.description: the failure copy when the server failed (5xx), in the visitor's words; plain text. Left out, {{FAILED_TEXT}} is shown

{{FAILED_HINT}}.description: alert.message under the failure title — what to do, e.g. Check the two fields and save again. Left out, the title stands alone

placeholders.{{SAVED_TEXT}}: alert.title once the step is saved, e.g. Your card is saved
placeholders.{{CURRENT_LABEL}}: text before the stored values, e.g. On your card now:
placeholders.{{LOAD_FAILED_TEXT}}: alert.message when the stored record could not be read (the form stays hidden so nothing is written twice), e.g. Your card did not load.

{{LOAD_FAILED_TITLE}}.description: alert.title over LOAD_FAILED_TEXT, e.g. This did not load. Left out, the message stands alone

placeholders.{{RETRY_LABEL}}: button.label that reads the stored record again, e.g. Try again

{{WIDTH}}.description: max-width of the card, a CSS length, e.g. 420px. Left out, the card takes the width of its column
